question.problem:
Let $A$ be a $2\times 2$ matrix with eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2$ corresponding to the eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ respectively, where

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Solve the following initial value problem:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 14\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Given a system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),
$$

where $A$ has two distinct eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1},{\lambda }_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2},$ the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our matrix differential equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$, we substitute $t=0$ in the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]{e}^{0}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{0} & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3{c}_{2} \\ 7{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 14\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}3{c}_{2}=0 \\ 7{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}=14.\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
{c}_{2}=0.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain 

$$
7{c}_{1}-0=14\,⟹\,{c}_{1}=2.
$$

 

Therefore, the solution for the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =2\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}+0\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 14\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}.\end{aligned}
$$
